title: Usage-driven model prioritization and scouting ops playbook
creator: Mariana Alvarez
description: Objective: Create an operational playbook that prioritizes candidate open models and vendor variants based on actual product usage patterns, economic sensitivity (per-token cost), and regional latency constraints. Deliverables: a prioritized model candidate ranking spreadsheet, a lightweight rubric for automated scoring from telemetry, a scout-runbook for nightly synthetic probes, and a field-probe plan for 3 pilot customers. This ticket focuses on the PM-side definition, coordinating with Applied ML (model-scouting), Observability (telemetry access), and Solutions (pilot customers).
acceptance_criteria: Scoring rubric defined and documented (latency sensitivity, cost elasticity, failure tolerance, feature parity) with weightings agreed by Eng+Applied ML
Automated telemetry feed (sampled anonymized usage patterns) mapped to rubric inputs in prototype spreadsheet
Scout-runbook produced: probe scripts, success/failure thresholds, regional probe schedule
Three pilot customers (internal or external) identified and signed off for field probes; outreach templates created
Handoff doc and 1-hour working session scheduled with Model Ops to operationalize periodic rescoring
updates: 2025-11-05 - Created ticket. Kickoff with Applied ML and Observability scheduled. Initial hypothesis: small-number high-volume routes drive >70% sensitivity to latency/cost tradeoffs.
2025-11-07 - Observability confirmed access to sampled route-level token counts and 95th percentile latency per route; agreed sample window = last 30 days. Next: define rubric inputs mapping.

2025-11-10 - Draft rubric shared (link to draft deck). Engineering raised concern about unstable signal for low-volume enterprise routes; added minimum-traffic floor and synthetic probe augmentation to compensate.
2025-11-12 - Decision to include two parallel signals: (1) telemetry-derived usage score, (2) synthetic probe stability score. Working on pilot customer list and outreach copy.
decisions: Use a dual-signal approach (usage telemetry + synthetic probes) to avoid false deprioritization of low-volume but critical enterprise routes.
Weightings for final score: 40% usage sensitivity, 30% latency risk, 20% cost elasticity, 10% feature/compatibility risk (initial weights subject to re-evaluation after pilot).
Minimum traffic floor set to 2000 tokens/day per route for pure telemetry scoring; below floor will rely primarily on probe stability and customer input.
risks: Telemetry gaps: regional sampling bias could misrank models for APAC-heavy customers.
Synthetic probes may not capture real-world prompt diversity leading to optimistic stability scores.
Customer recruitment: pilot customers may be hesitant to run probes that alter SLA-backed routes without clear rollback guarantees.
next_steps: Finalize rubric and convert to a small computation notebook that consumes sampled telemetry (owner: Liam) - target 2025-11-18
Prepare synthetic probe set (50 canonical prompts per route class) and run nightly for two weeks in eu-west and us-west (owner: Applied ML - Priya) - start 2025-11-15
Identify and confirm 3 pilot customers; prepare non-invasive field probe plan and rollback protocol (owner: Solutions - Hana) - complete by 2025-11-20
Share interim findings and proposed prioritization with GTM for feedback (meeting scheduled 2025-11-22)
